import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('data/housing_dataset.csv')

# Data preparation
# Convert categorical to numeric for correlation analysis (mainroad, guestroom, etc.)
categorical_cols = ['mainroad', 'guestroom', 'basement', 'hotwaterheating', 'airconditioning', 'prefarea']
for col in categorical_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].map({'yes': 1, 'no': 0})

print('Summary Stats:')
print(df['price'].describe())

# Correlation analysis
correlations = df.select_dtypes(include='number').corr()['price'].sort_values(ascending=False)
print('\nCorrelation with Price:')
print(correlations)

# Create Figures
# 1. Area vs Price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='area', y='price')
plt.title('Housing Price vs. Total Area')
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
plt.savefig('charts/price_vs_area.png')

# 2. Furnishing Status impact
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x='furnishingstatus', y='price', data=df, palette='viridis')
plt.title('Price Distribution by Furnishing Status')
plt.savefig('charts/furnishing_impact.png')

# 3. Multi-variate impact (Bedrooms & Bathrooms)
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='bedrooms', y='price', hue='bathrooms', palette='coolwarm', size='area', sizes=(20, 200))
plt.title('Price vs Bedrooms & Bathrooms')
plt.savefig('charts/rooms_impact.png')

# 4. Amenity Impact (Hot Water / AC)
features = ['mainroad', 'guestroom', 'basement', 'hotwaterheating', 'airconditioning']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15,10))
axes_flat = axes.flatten()
for i, feature in enumerate(features):
    sns.barplot(x=feature, y='price', data=df, ax=axes_flat[i])
    axes_flat[i].set_title(f'Impact: {feature}')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('charts/amenities_impact.png')

# Hide the 6th empty plot if it exists (since we only have 5 features)
axes_flat[-1].axis('off')
plt.savefig('charts/amenities_impact.png') # save again after cleanup

print('Plots generated successfully.')

python3 -c "
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('data/housing_dataset.csv')

# Analysis for reporting
print(f'Total Records: {len(df)}')
print('Price Mean:', df['price'].mean())
# Correlation of key features
correlations = df.select_dtypes(include='number').corr()['price'].sort_values(ascending=False)
print('\nCorrelations with Price:')
print(correlations)

# Plotting logic - since seaborn might not be available, use standard matplotlib/pandas plotting
# 1. Area vs Price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
plt.scatter(df['area'], df['price'], alpha=0.5)
plt.title('Price vs Area')
plt.xlabel('Area (sqft)')
plt.ylabel('Price')
plt.savefig('charts/price_vs_area.png')

# 2. Furnishing Status impact
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
furnish_means = df.groupby('furnishingstatus')['price'].mean()
furnish_means.plot(kind='bar', color='skyblue')
plt.title('Average Price by Furnishing Status')
plt.ylabel('Mean Price')
plt.savefig('charts/furnishing_impact.png')

# 3. Rooms comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
# We can't easily use 'hue' in basic matplotlib without extra work, so we'll do a grouped bar for room types or something simple
rooms = df.groupby(['bedrooms', 'bathrooms'])['price'].mean().unstack()
rooms.plot(kind='bar')
plt.title('Avg Price by Bedroom/Bathroom Count')
plt.ylabel('Mean Price')
plt.savefig('charts/rooms_impact.png')

# 4. Amenities impact
amenities = ['mainroad', 'guestroom', 'basement', 'hotwaterheating', 'airconditioning']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15,10))
axes_flat = axes.flatten()
for i, am in enumerate(amenities):
    # Group by the "yes/no" or numeric (if we converted) - here they are strings
    group_means = df.groupby(am)['price'].mean()
    group_means.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes_flat[i], color='orange')
    axes_flat[i].set_title(f'Impact of {am}')
    axes_flat[i].set_ylim(df['price'].min(), df['price'].max())

# Hide the last plot
axes_flat[5].axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('charts/amenities_impact.png')

print('All figures saved.')

import pandas as pd
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt

# Define the presentation content structure
slides_data = [
    ('Housing Market Analysis', 'Key Insights, Drivers, and Recommendations\nData Analytics Report'),
    ('Dataset Overview', [
        'Total Dataset Size: 545 Records',
        'Main metric analyzed: Property Price',
        'Primary Features:',
        '- Physical (Area, Bedrooms, Bathrooms, Stories)',
        '- Amenities (Mainroad, Guestroom, Basement, Hot Water, AC)',
        '- Status (Parking capacity, Furnishing status)'
    ]),
    ('Key Market Trends', [
        'Size Correlation: Area and Bathrooms are the strongest predictors of price.',
        'Amenity Premium: Properties with \"Mainroad\" access command a significant premium.',
        'Furnishing Impact: Furnished units consistently outperform semi-furnished/unfurnished ones in valuation.',
        'Scale Variance: Significant variation in pricing for properties over 10,000 sq. ft.'
    ]),
    ('Key Drivers of Price', [
        'Physical Scale: Area (Corr: 0.536) and Bathrooms (0.517) are top factors.',
        'Accessibility: Main road status is a major categorical driver.',
        'Amenity Boosts: Hot water, AC, and Guest rooms provide consistent marginal gains.',
        'Complexity Factor: Story count (Corr: 0.421) shows strong secondary impact.'
    ]),
    ('Business Recommendations', [
        'Inventory Strategy: Prioritize \"Ready-to-Move\" (Fully Furnished) units for premium targeting.',
        'Development Focus: High bathroom counts and multi-story designs offer the best ROI/sq. ft.',
        'Marketing Pivot: Highlight \"Main Road\" accessibility as a primary selling point in advertising.',
        'Upsell Opportunity: Include high-demand amenities (AC, Hot Water) as standard features to maintain valuation.'
    ])
]

# Create presentation
prs = Presentation()

# Handle Title Slide (Slide Layout 0)
title_slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
title_slide.shapes.title.text = slides_data[0][0]
title_slide.placeholders[1].text = slides_data[0][1]

# Handle Content Slides (Slide Layout 1)
for i in range(1, len(slides_data)):
    slide_content = slides_data[i]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
    slide.shapes.title.text = slide_content[0]
    
    # Add bullets
    body_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
    tf = body_shape.text_frame
    for item in slide_content[1]:
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = item
        p.level = 0

prs.save('housing_analysis.pptx')
print('File housing_analysis.pptx created successfully.')
